title: Encyclopaedia Britannica - Seventh edition, Volume 21, Surveying-ZYM - EB.15
text: context. In this passage, as in the former instance, the word _pledes_ precedes meznazini, both words being brought together, and occurring in a parallelism. The passage referred to is rendered in our version, "who hath weighed the mountain in scales, and the hills in a balance." The word here rendered scales of the plurals, is the singular noun _pheles ;_ while that rendered balance, is the dual word _mazain._ The English therefore would better accord with the original, were the term in the translation reversed in order, and read thus: " who hath weighed the mountain in a balance, and the little scales".
